runners_data.name: Silky Robin
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with her best form at 5f on good ground (win at 5f/GOO in recent hist), sporting a hood; Jason Watson takes the ride for trainer Brian Toomey who has had no runners in the past 14 days, and the 34-day absence is worth noting, though her style-fit score signals she is already at the sharp end of her optimal role.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by half a length at Lingfield last time from a 5lb lower mark, and the top course jockey aboard is a clear asset; drawn 4 and equipped with first-time blinkers today. The concern is whether the new mark leaves sufficient room, but the recent form is live.

runners_data.name: Desdemona
runners_data.note: Luke Morris partners this hold-up filly who carries a tongue-tie and has two wins at 5f on standard ground in her last five, trainer Attwater has seven runners in the past 14 days suggesting yard is in form, and her sim-going record is modest (1W1P from 15) which is a mild caution on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces are applied and the course and distance are familiar, but Desdemona was tardy at the start last time and made no impression, beaten four lengths at Lingfield off a 2lb higher mark; our figures rank her last in the field. Needs considerably more.

runners_data.name: Recon Mission
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's ten-year-old veteran has solid good-ground placed form (2nd and 3rd in recent GOO runs) and Carson takes the ride; by nature a hold-up horse who will want to drop in and come late, though the redistribution note reflects that the rear is congested and he may not find the gaps he needs in a small field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts but attracts the top course trainer, who has a strong record here, and Recon Mission has sound experience over today's trip and going; a placed effort is within the recent form. Two below-par runs in a row, however, need to be reversed.

runners_data.name: Harry Brown
runners_data.note: Darragh Keenan partners this six-year-old who landed a 5f/GOO win last time out and claims notable Brighton-specific form; despite that recent win, he is a genuine hold-up type whose map position has been pushed forward — his chances depend on whether the race pace is strong enough to bring him into contention in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Acquitted himself well when fourth last time, beaten two lengths in a class 5 event, and arrives here 1lb lower — course and distance are proven and our figures put him clear of this field. Did pull keen on that occasion, but the overall profile strongly supports another forward showing.

runners_data.name: Marra Donna
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly for Ollie Sangster and Donohoe, with a 2nd at 5f/STA and 3rd at 6f/STA in recent form, though her sim-going record is bare (0W0P from 10 on comparable ground) and her best effort came on soft, making the fast surface a genuine query.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces are applied and the course is familiar, but Marra Donna is winless in recent starts and trailed home ninth here last time; ideally needs further than today's 6f and a strong pace to deliver her best. Hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Havana Jag
runners_data.note: Unraced for 102 days — the longest break in the field — for trainer John Gallagher, with a three-race run of 3rd-4th-4th suggesting consistency without a win, and a style marked unknown; the 3-lb claimer Jack Callan partners, and his ability to settle quickly and find a rhythm off a front-runner could determine how effective the return is.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who has finished in the frame across recent starts and acts on good to firm; back after 102 days away, which is the obvious question mark on return. Last time at Newcastle was flat over a stiff 5f when used prominently, and today's course may suit a more patient approach.

races.paceDynamic: Silky Robin is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, should control proceedings from the front at a rhythm entirely of her own choosing on good-to-firm ground over 5½f at Brighton. The hold-up contingent — Desdemona, Recon Mission, Harry Brown, and Marra Donna — are all closers by nature, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured from the gate and Silky Robin can bowl along uncontested. Recon Mission and Harry Brown are genuine hold-up horses that the map has redistributed to midfield, as the rear of the field is more crowded with closers than the visual positions suggest; neither is likely to secure a prominent berth naturally. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or a horse racing prominently just off the lead, as the absence of early pressure creates a steady, controlled gallop that makes closers' tasks harder and gives a confirmed leader a significant tactical edge.

watchPoints.text: Silky Robin's break from the stalls is critical — if she misses the kick and surrenders the lead, the entire race shape collapses and hold-up horses instantly become more dangerous.

Desdemona's tongue-tie and good recent form at 5f for an in-form yard make her the most potent closer if the pace eases sufficiently; watch how quickly Luke Morris moves her into contention from the 2f pole.

Harry Brown won last time on good ground at 5f but is a natural hold-up type — watch whether Keenan tries to position him more prominently than his style suggests, as it could compromise his finishing effort.

Havana Jag's 102-day absence is the longest in the field; watch his early movement for any signs of ring-rustiness, as unknown style combined with a long layoff introduces an element of unpredictability to the race shape.

The entire field runs on going officially recorded as Good To Firm — faster than the header states Good — which may sharpen early fractions and suit the confirmed front-runner more than the closing style of the majority of this field.

runners_data.name: Henley On Thames
runners_data.comment: Debut at Sandown offered encouragement — showed early pace and the sixth-place finish left plenty of room for progress — and improvement is expected second time out. Fading late is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Ava Louise
runners_data.comment: Pedigree appeals: a Territories filly and half-sister to a very smart 6f performer, with the top course jockey in the saddle. Unraced, though, and likely to need this debut outing before producing her best.

runners_data.name: Clueisinthetitle
runners_data.comment: Well held on debut at Chepstow, trailing the principals by a distance, and requires a major step forward to feature here; lightly raced at least leaves some scope, but the evidence to date gives little to work with.

runners_data.name: Roxa Love
runners_data.comment: Finished with a clear surge when third on debut at Lingfield, shaped with clear promise over today's trip on good to firm, and the trainer is in excellent current form at 26% in the last fortnight. Yet to go one better, but this is comfortably the most compelling profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Targa
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths in a novice last time yet did more than the result suggests and looks the type to take a forward step; has experience of today's course and going. Back-to-back below-par efforts mean improvement is essential.

runners_data.name: Dupont Circle
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse whose trainer Benton has a poor 14-day record (0/4) and whose last two runs at 7-8f on soft/standard suggest this 1m4f good-to-firm trip is an entirely different proposition; the ⚠ fade flag is a red light in a race likely to finish in a sprint|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and has been disappointing across three outings — well down the field at Salisbury most recently — and needs a significant jump in form. The course and distance are not the issue, so the trainer will be hoping for a better showing.

runners_data.name: Fighting Poet
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old gelding with genuine 10f good-ground form including two placings at similar trips — Sean Bowen is a sharp jockey who may take matters into his own hands in a leaderless race; though technically a hold-up horse by profile, the redistribution note reflects he could be forced into an unnatural midfield role if others also hang back|
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers applied and has experience over today's trip and going, with some decent form earlier in the season; but Fighting Poet made no impression when well beaten here most recently and is yet to score in recent starts. Must improve considerably to get involved.

runners_data.name: Foinix
runners_data.note: Jim and Suzi Best's six-year-old has the widest stamina profile in the field with a run at 16f, giving it a potential advantage if the race is anything but a sprint; blinkers fitted, and while its recent form reads 27-877, a genuinely run 1m4f on good could unlock better|
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers are interesting for Foinix and there is a placed effort within recent form over this sort of trip; acts on fast ground and handles the course. That said, the last four runs have all produced well-beaten efforts and more is clearly needed to contend.

runners_data.name: Gearing's Point
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday (LR:1d) which is a significant freshness concern, though the horse has been placed at 12f on good ground twice in five runs and Sheena West clearly believes it is race-fit; a natural hold-up type forced into midfield mapping, but its recent form at this exact trip and going makes it the most relevant course-and-distance runner|
runners_data.comment: In solid form prior to the latest — placed twice in the recent past — and handles today's going; first-time cheekpieces fitted and stays the trip. The concern is that Gearing's Point over-raced and weakened sharply at Leicester last time, so a more restrained approach will be needed.

runners_data.name: Highland Harvey
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old with the ⚠ fade flag and a trainer 14-day strike rate of 1/7 suggesting no particular angle; placed twice at 12f on standard and good but has shown a tendency to weaken late, which is a concern in a race that is likely to compress into a sprint finish demanding a sharp kick|
runners_data.comment: Consistent form with placed efforts across recent starts and proven over today's going; yet to score but rarely far away and the profile is competitive in a race of this nature. The 102-day absence since Newcastle is the main unknown on return.

runners_data.name: Sweetstevie
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and carries the fade flag — in a contest that will almost certainly be decided over the final two furlongs, the tendency to weaken late is a significant negative; best form a second at 10f on soft, and the step up in trip to 1m4f on quick ground looks speculative|
runners_data.comment: A first-time visor prompted a clear step up last time when a close second at Yarmouth — the best effort in recent starts — and effective at 10f on slower ground; the headgear is retained today. The question is whether that uplift can be sustained.

runners_data.name: Dream Of Ithaca
runners_data.note: Luke Morris's 3-year-old carries just 121lbs against a field of older rivals on 135lbs — a 14lb weight advantage that could matter enormously in a closely-run sprint finish; five runs at 10-12f with mid-division finishes, and trainer Gallagher has one winner from six in the last fortnight, suggesting stable is in some form|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Windsor last time and has struggled for form across five recent outings; Dream Of Ithaca handles 10f and sound surfaces could help, but all to prove before this one can be taken seriously.

runners_data.name: Hello Garda
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's 3-year-old has been beaten a long way in three runs at 8-10f on good, and the trainer's dismal 14-day record (0/15) offers no encouragement; also carries the fade flag and has had 21 days off — the step up to 1m4f is unproven and the previous form is very weak, making this hard to support|
runners_data.comment: A respected Irish yard and a top course jockey are positives, and Hello Garda is the type that may do better with experience. Three runs have all been modest so far, but there is reason to believe improvement is on the cards.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this eight-horse field carrying a hold-up or rear-of-field profile, there is no confirmed front runner and no horse with a natural desire to lead — meaning the early gallop at Brighton's 1m4f trip will almost certainly be pedestrian, with runners jostling cautiously before the pace ignites on the long climb to the home turn. The race is therefore likely to be run as a slowly-run drift into a sprint finish up the straight, favouring whoever can produce the sharpest late kick rather than any ability to sustain pressure from the front. Gearing's Point, Fighting Poet, and Sweetstevie have all been flagged as genuine prominent or hold-up types who may push forward to fill the leadership vacuum when no natural front runner asserts, but in a field of eight reluctant pacers, the jockey who commits earliest takes a real tactical gamble. This shape heavily favours the horse with the cleanest finishing speed over the final two furlongs rather than one with stamina or tactical nous, making an angled late challenge from the inside the most likely winning move on Brighton's undulating track.

runners_data.name: Joycean Way
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid recent form showing two 3rds on good ground; Gary & Josh Moore yard in decent nick at 4/31 over 14 days and David Egan takes the ride — best sim-going record in the field at 7/15 with four places suggesting consistent competitiveness, and the step up to 1m2f from recent 8f runs should suit.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third here last time, going down by one and a quarter lengths off a 1lb higher mark — the strongest piece of recent form in this field; course and going are familiar and a first-time hood is fitted today. Yet to score, but the profile represents a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: D Day Major Winter
runners_data.note: 277 days off the track is the dominant concern here — layoff of that length on a return at a stiff Brighton 1m2f in fast ground demands significant fitness; placed twice at 10f on good ground so the trip is no issue, but the hold-up style with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 means it is racing out of its natural role and its chance must be tempered accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Absent for the best part of nine months and arrives equipped with a first-time hood; trainer is in good current form and D Day Major Winter has placed form over this trip on fast ground. Very difficult to assess off such a lengthy break, and inconsistency throughout the record adds to the question marks.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton yard is in form at 4/33 over 14 days and Callum Hutchinson claims; the mare has shown no win form across six runs and no places on good ground specifically (0W0P), and while she is likely to race more prominently than her nominal style suggests, the form figures of 43-466 do not inspire confidence.|
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces may sharpen things up for a horse that has placed form at this going and is capable of better than the last two outings; winless in recent starts but generally a solid performer when at her best. Needs to recapture that form to feature.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Class
runners_data.note: Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole partnership lands a 3-year-old who has placed at 10f on good ground, directly relevant to this trip; Jack Callan's 3lb claim helps offset the weights, but the horse's true hold-up style mapped to midfield carries a STYLE_FIT of 0.90, and just 1/7 sim-going runs with one place underlines the limited evidence base.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Chepstow last time, beaten two and a quarter lengths at this exact mark over the trip, makes Dash Of Class's form credentials clear; acts on good to firm and a first-time hood adds a further positive. The strongest profile in this race and the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Dora Vita
runners_data.note: Richard Phillips has just 1/4 over 14 days and the form string of 044060 is frankly weak — a finishing position of 13th from 8f on good ground last time is a red flag; the fades-in-finish flag is particularly damaging in a race where the decisive moment will come sharply in the final two furlongs, and the hold-up redistribution only compounds the concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless across six recent starts and well beaten at Windsor last time; Dora Vita acts on AW and may be better suited by stepping up to a mile, but neither condition applies today. Hard to make a case from the current form.

runners_data.name: Diamond Aura
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer is in excellent form at 4/51 over 14 days and Luke Morris is experienced, but five consecutive finishes in the 5th-to-8th range on standard tracks with a fades-in-finish flag make this a very hard horse to trust; the Brighton 1m2f on fast ground should theoretically suit if she settles and travels, yet the form evidence consistently shows she finds little when it matters.|
runners_data.comment: First-time hood fitted but Diamond Aura has failed to produce anything convincing across recent starts, beaten ten lengths at Chepstow last time; last on our figures and needs to reverse a consistent run of poor efforts before being taken seriously.

races.paceDynamic: This is a six-runner field at Brighton over 1m2f in Good to Firm conditions with no confirmed front-runner — every declared runner carries a hold-up or prominent tag, meaning the pace will almost certainly be modest from the outset and the race will compress into a tactical drift before erupting into a sprint finish up Brighton's distinctive undulating straight. With no horse willing to take ownership of the race from the front, the early furlongs will be tentative, creating a bunched, slow-burn scenario where positioning through the final bend becomes critical. The entire field is effectively Hold-Up in profile, meaning those who can travel smoothly through the pack and produce a sharp finish from the belly of the race will be best placed — closers who genuinely stay the 1m2f trip and accelerate on fast ground hold the clearest edge. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, with Joycean Way and Beryl's Girl the most likely to at least attempt to race with more purpose and secure an advantageous early position.

runners_data.name: The Bitter Moose
runners_data.note: Last won over 7f on Good ground 23 days ago and that course/going form reads well here; genuine hold-up runner who will be ridden patiently by Neil Callan and needs a strong enough gallop to finish off — the modest pace is the primary concern, but headgear (visor) and a 9/15 record on similar going suggest he is in decent fettle.
runners_data.comment: Third at Lingfield most recently, beaten four and a half lengths, and acts well on sharp tracks over today's sort of trip; generally consistent and the first-time visor is a new angle. Ranked fifth on our figures, though, and must step up to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Lunario
runners_data.note: Luke Dace's six-year-old is another confirmed hold-up type whose recent form (8th, 9th, 7th) makes the overall profile look weak, but two wins on similar going over this trip give him some credibility; the claim of Jack Dace (5lb) is a minor cost offset, and the 21-day break after a string of modest efforts means improvement is possible if the race develops his way.
runners_data.comment: Mark is easing which is mildly encouraging, and the trip and going are familiar, but Lunario has been out of form for a long stretch — five consecutive defeats including two where never involved — and the form line gives little reason for optimism. Must be taken on trust.

runners_data.name: State Of Madness
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old ran just three days ago and drops from 6f to 7f, which on the face of it looks awkward, but he has three placed efforts over this trip and Luke Morris can ride him prominently — his role is to sit just behind Tea Sea and apply whatever pressure he can, though his trainer's 0/16 over 14 days tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Consistent at this level, handles course and distance comfortably, and is only 1lb above the last winning mark; acts on any ground and is a genuine threat. The quick turnaround — racing just three days ago — is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Tea Sea
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's mare is the only dedicated front-runner and will be allowed to set her own terms by William Carson; a STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 reflects that she is technically listed as prominent but is operating in a near-ideal lead scenario here, and her one win over 7f on Good ground with the blinker fitted is directly relevant — the warning is that she has struggled to win in 2026 and the non-winner restriction confirms recent form is modest.
runners_data.comment: Landed a course-and-distance success in recent form and the top course trainer is a significant positive; acts on a sound surface and the first-time blinkers may well sharpen the response. Last time at Brighton was a step back — beaten nine lengths over a longer trip — so returning to today's distance looks the right move.

runners_data.name: Middleton View
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' four-year-old has a headgear combination (hood/tongue tie) and a 33-day break since her last run, and she is a true hold-up runner placed in midfield on the map purely because the field is saturated with closers; her 0W0P record in similar going conditions is a stark negative, and despite Jack Callan's 3lb claim the form profile gives little reason to upgrade her chances.
runners_data.comment: Placed over 7f last time, beaten two lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Yarmouth, and is nicely below the last winning mark — the profile is appealing in a field of this nature; acts on good and AW and the first-time hood-and-tongue combination may help. Winless in recent starts remains the main caveat.

runners_data.name: King Of War
runners_data.note: David Egan's booking for Michael Wigham's seven-year-old is the standout jockey-horse pairing for a late run — two wins over 7f on Good ground from five attempts is a strong conversion rate, and the tongue-piece plus pads suggest connections know what they need; like Middleton View, he is a genuine hold-up horse re-mapped to midfield, but Egan's race-reading ability makes him the most likely of the redistributed runners to find his true position and deliver a finish.
runners_data.comment: In good form of late and placed at this course over a mile last time, beaten just two lengths off the same mark — course and going are clearly to his liking. Suited by 7f and fast ground, and a first-time tongue-strap and hood combination may sharpen the response.

races.paceDynamic: Tea Sea is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's 7f, is likely to bowl along uncontested at a sustainable, metronomic gallop — William Carson will be able to dictate terms from the front without any genuine challenger for the lead. State Of Madness is the only other prominent-style runner and will sit just off Tea Sea's shoulder, but neither horse has the profile to force a burning early pace that would blow the race apart. With no credible pace duel in prospect, the tempo is likely to be controlled and steady, suiting horses who can track the leader and quicken from a good position rather than deep closers who need a strong gallop to reel the front runner in. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with finishing pace, but critically, Middleton View and King Of War — both genuine hold-up types — have been redistributed to midfield in the map because the field holds more come-from-behind runners than the visual rear can accommodate; of those two, King Of War (David Egan, proven 7f Good form, two wins in similar conditions) is the more likely to actually secure a tracking midfield berth and benefit.

watchPoints.text: Tea Sea's ability to lead unchallenged is the single biggest shape factor — watch the first furlong to see if State Of Madness pushes for the front, because any pressure on Tea Sea would fundamentally alter the pace and the race outcome.

King Of War and Middleton View are both genuine hold-up horses competing for the same late ground; if they are both trapped behind a wall with nowhere to go in Brighton's tight straight, neither may get a clear run — watch for traffic at the two-furlong pole.

The Bitter Moose finished 1st at 7f Good just 23 days ago, making him potentially the freshest and sharpest closer in the field — if Tea Sea's gallop is slow enough, Neil Callan may look to make earlier headway than his style suggests, which would change his profile entirely.

State Of Madness ran only three days ago — watch for any signs of fatigue in the closing stages, particularly if he has burned energy trying to match strides with Tea Sea early on; Luke Morris may choose to drop him in and conserve energy rather than force the pace.

runners_data.name: Aim For The Bull
runners_data.note: Progressive form (two wins in last six, including a recent course-relevant win over 8f on Good), prominent racer suited by this trip, Jack Callan 3lb claim is useful, and the visor headgear should keep it focused; 24 days between runs is fine.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time, getting up by a neck, and clearly handles this course and trip well; three wins in recent starts underline the form and today's ground is fine. First-time hood fitted, but carrying a full weight at the top of the handicap will make it harder to repeat.

runners_data.name: Havana Mojito
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter in this field; Luke Morris partners, John Gallagher yard in modest form (1/6 T14), and it is effectively racing out of its natural role as a prominent type — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 means discount its chance if pressed.
runners_data.comment: Pushed very close here last time in first-time blinkers, beaten a neck off this mark — the form is right there and the course holds no fears. Yet to score in recent starts but has left no doubt about the ability, and a repeat of that effort could be enough.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 6f and 7f on Good ground make it the standout course-and-distance form horse; genuine hold-up style and the trip suits, though at 7 years old it needs to produce at the right moment — Darragh Keenan is a positive booking.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive wins, including a smooth success at Bath last time where the cheekpieces clearly galvanised the form; acts on all going types and has course-and-distance experience. Going for a hat-trick off a competitive mark, but the recent consistency makes the case hard to resist.

runners_data.name: Bear To Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been inconsistent at this trip (best runs at 8f), Mason Paetel's 5lb claim helps offset the weight, but trainer Michael Attwater has had no strikes in seven runners over 14 days — form is patchy.
runners_data.comment: Placed second at Lingfield earlier in the season and handles the course and trip on a sound surface; was in fair form prior. Most recently, though, Bear To Dream was ridden to see out the trip and found it all too much, beaten over seven lengths, and needs a stronger pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Zu Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose last run was a creditable second over 7f on Good; Paddy Bradley takes over, trainer Loughnane without a hit in 16 runners over 14 days is a concern, but the horse clearly handles this trip and going.
runners_data.comment: Close up at Brighton last time, beaten three lengths off a 1lb lower mark, and the course and going are familiar; first-time hood fitted and acts over 7f on fast ground. Drawn in stall 12 and yet to score in recent starts — those are the main obstacles.

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, no wins from recent Brighton attempts, trainer James Owen in excellent T14 form (12/60) which is the main angle; only 11 days since last run and a switch to 7f from 6f last time could help — no Going concern.
runners_data.comment: Good second at Yarmouth last time, beaten one and a half lengths off this mark, represents solid recent evidence and the course and trip are both proven; first-time tongue-tie is an additional angle. Yet to score in recent starts, but the trend is clearly upward.

runners_data.name: Amathus
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with extensive form on Good ground (ten of last 15 runs) but struggling for wins of late; placed twice over 8f on Good but Brighton's 7f may not fully suit a horse that prefers a little more time to land his blow.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Lingfield in fair form earlier in the campaign and handles this course and going; first-time visor could be a catalyst. Last time at Bath, though, barely figured at any stage, beaten four lengths, and needs to recapture that earlier promise to get involved.

runners_data.name: Oh So Audacious
runners_data.note: David Egan rides and this horse has excellent Good-ground form (13/15 runs), winning once over this exact course and distance; prominent style is perfectly suited to the expected race shape and 28 days since last run is no worry.
runners_data.comment: Has landed a win in recent form and knows this course, trip and going well; effective at 7-8f on a sound surface. The most recent outing was well below that level — beaten ten lengths from off the pace at Leicester — so a significant upturn in form is needed before this one can be taken seriously.

runners_data.name: Henry Tudor
runners_data.note: Strong-finishing hold-up type by nature, but the redistribution note is honest — the map shows it in midfield because it cannot get to the rear in this field; Ashley Lewis's 5lb claim is the main positive, and sim-going figures are modest (1/11 on firm-ish ground).
runners_data.comment: Has a win in recent starts and course experience, but the last two outings have both produced big defeats, most recently beaten six lengths here from off the pace; usually held up and the wide draw in stall 10 will not help. Needs to recapture that form sharply.

runners_data.name: Daley T
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll yard is very active (11/52 T14), and William Carson rides with experience; naturally wants to come from well off the pace but is mapped centrally given the hold-up traffic, meaning its true late-finishing style (STYLE_FIT 0.90) is compromised in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Top course trainer connected and the stable has a strong record at Brighton; Daley T posted a quarter-length third here most recently, tried in cheekpieces. Inconsistent and yet to score in recent starts, though, and must improve on the figures to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Maury
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard but Good-ground credentials are limited (5/14 sim-going); a true hold-up runner who is pushed into the midfield picture by field congestion — Kieren Fox partners, but the positional compromise makes this hard to fancy off OR 48.
runners_data.comment: Has a win to the name in recent form and is effective at 7-8f, but last time out was a near-historic reversal — beaten thirty-five lengths — and that form is extremely hard to look past. Still to prove the ability transfers to turf.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: Gary and Josh Moore yard has been active (4/31 T14); showed placed form at 7f on Good but the redistribution into midfield means its natural closing style is partially neutralised — Finley Marsh rides and the lowest OR in the field (47) is the key hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Two placed efforts earlier in the season and acts on a wide range of surfaces; Bated Breeze handles 6-7f and the course is familiar. A well-beaten effort here last time is a concern and a wide draw in stall 11 does not help — needs to recapture earlier form.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Mojito is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival prepared to press it hard from the off, it should control an honest but sustainable gallop over Brighton's 7f on Good to Firm ground. Aim For The Bull, Bear To Dream, and Oh So Audacious will press forward into prominent positions, creating a small cluster of pace-forward horses behind the leader but no all-out war for the front. The result is a race that sets up at a measured, even tempo — enough to stretch the field but not so brutal that front-runners are cooked entering the final two furlongs. This shape squarely favours horses that can track the pace from a prominent or close-stalking position and produce a clean, sustained run to the line, rather than closers forced wide or late off a slow burn; several true hold-up types — Henry Tudor, Daley T, Maury, and Bated Breeze — cannot realistically get their natural rear position given the volume of hold-up horses in this field, and among the prominent brigade, Aim For The Bull and Oh So Audacious are best placed to secure the positions that suit them.

watchPoints.text: Havana Mojito's ability to get a clear lead unchallenged is pivotal — if Aim For The Bull or Oh So Audacious push up early and deny it a settled rhythm, the entire pace scenario shifts and the sustainable lead evaporates.

Dion Baker is the most dangerous hold-up threat: back-to-back wins on Good, suited by the trip, and Darragh Keenan's booking is purposeful — monitor its position leaving the stalls if the field bunches.

Oh So Audacious has excellent Good-ground form (13/15) and David Egan's tactical intelligence at Brighton makes it a quiet danger if it settles just off the pace — watch for it being produced widest of the prominent group entering the final furlong.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Henry Tudor, Daley T, Maury, Bated Breeze) all forced into midfield creates potential traffic issues in the straight — a late stumbling block for any genuine late finisher in a compacted field.

Trainer James Owen's T14 strike rate (12/60) for Prefer The Sister is unusually strong and worth monitoring in the market — if it drifts, the angle loses credibility; if it firms, Owen may know something about how the horse will handle the 7f trip.
